# DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731

> A zero-dependency vanilla-JS Pokedex on Cloudflare Workers whose strength is its data pipeline: scripts/ingest.js pulls all 1025 species plus every referenced move, ability, item and type from PokeAPI with pooled concurrency, retries and resume-on-restart, transforms them into compact payloads and writes chunked bulk NDJSON that is loaded into KV; src/index.ts then serves nine JSON endpoints straight from KV with batched multi-key gets and s-maxage/stale-while-revalidate headers, so nothing hits PokeAPI at request time. The split is stark: the worker and the ingest script are production-shaped, while the 1105-line public/app.js carries the defects — a mis-wired reference that makes the Matchups tab render the literal word 'undefined' in all 36 rows for every species, offensive type effectiveness computed as a product of the attacker's own two types, a search that cannot find the hyphenated names it prints itself, and method chips that show a fraction of each learnset. It covers the core dex competently (full 1025 browse verified live, filters, an excellent stats tab, a recursive branching evolution tree, compare) and stops there: no team builder, damage calculator, standalone moves dex, type chart, minigame, command palette or export, and no alternate forms at all because ingest hard-filters to ids 1-1025.

## Strengths

- Data architecture: a resume-safe pooled ingest (ingest.js:56 pool, ingest.js:94 skip-already-done, ingest.js:30 retry/backoff) feeding chunked bulk KV writes, with the worker doing batched multi-key KV reads (src/index.ts:40-56, capped at 64) behind real cache-control headers — the whole dataset is prebuilt and runtime has zero PokeAPI dependency.
- The worker and its type model are the best-written code in the submission: strict-TS dispatch with typed KV reads, regex-bounded id validation, per-route 404s, a single try/catch 500, SPA fallback and `satisfies ExportedHandler<Env>` (src/index.ts), against a hand-written 128-line domain model (src/types.ts).
- The stats tab matches the exceptional anchor: double-rAF animated per-stat bars with per-stat gradients plus a hand-built SVG radar (app.js:628) with rings, axis lines, polar maths, labels and a gradient fill, plus BST and average.
- Evolution is genuinely branching and thoroughly labelled: parseNode recurses over evolves_to mapping every evolution_details entry (ingest.js:321), and parseTrigger hand-writes 13 trigger kinds including Legends-Arceus mechanics (agile/strong style, tower-of-darkness, three-critical-hits) with time-of-day, rain and location suffixes — Eevee renders all 8 branches with 6 distinct triggers on Leafeon.

## Weaknesses

- The Matchups tab ships a mis-wired reference: tag is written as (m) => m.t but called as tag(t) with a string (app.js:848,851,853), and TYPE_ICON — a function — is indexed as an object, so all 36 rows render a grey badge reading 'undefined' with no type name. tsconfig.json scopes typecheck to src/** only, so the file containing the bug is never type-checked, and smoke.mjs screenshots the tab without asserting content.
- Offensive type effectiveness is computed wrong: app.js:835 multiplies the Pokemon's own two types together against each defender, so Charizard is shown at 4x into grass and bug instead of two separate 2x STAB options. The defensive table (app.js:823) is correct, including 0x immunities.
- Search cannot find the names the app itself renders — cards display 'ho oh' (app.js:272) while matchesSearch tests the raw 'ho-oh' (app.js:176), so all 76 hyphenated species return zero for their displayed name.
- Learnset method chips are truncated by design: app.js:751 assigns each move a single bucket by priority, so on Charizard 88 of 131 multi-method moves are missing from every chip but their highest-priority one.
- No alternate forms at all — ingest.js:88 filters to ids 1-1025, so mega/Gigantamax/regional varieties are never fetched.
- Mobile browse is rough at the most common phone width: measured at 390x844 the grid collapses to one column while a never-collapsing sticky topbar plus 18 wrapped type chips and 3 selects eat ~40% of the viewport, and the sticky offsets are hardcoded 10px short (.filters-wrap top:55px against a 65px topbar, styles.css:142; .detail-tabs top:53px against a 65px head, styles.css:345), clipping the first chip row behind the bar on every screen.
- Accessibility stops at the surface: the modal never moves focus in and has no focus trap, role=tab buttons carry no aria-selected/aria-controls, single-select type chips are role=checkbox, and the sprite-mode select's only label is an .sr-only class that is never defined in the stylesheet.
- Real dead weight for a one-shot build: a tautological filter (ingest.js:113), a per-Pokemon typeInfo blob written into all 1025 KV values (ingest.js:443) that the client never reads (it calls /api/types instead), METHOD_ORDER and state.typesData defined and never used, buildTypeChips() called twice in init (app.js:1056,1088), dead .matchup-grid and .skeleton CSS.
- init() (app.js:1052) has no catch around the initial /api/pokemon + /api/meta fetch, so a failed cold load leaves a silently empty grid with no error state.
- Filter/search/sort state lives only in localStorage, never in the URL, so no filtered view is shareable.
- Every image and cry is hotlinked to raw.githubusercontent.com (ingest.js:14,182) rather than an asset CDN or R2, and the data/ + KV-upload last mile is gitignored, so the pipeline is not reproducible from the repo alone.

## Standout

The ingest-to-KV pipeline in scripts/ingest.js — pooled fetching with per-item retries, resume by skipping already-written files, a secondary phase that fetches only the moves/abilities/items actually referenced, and chunked bulk NDJSON output — is a genuinely production-shaped data build, and it sits in the same repo as a frontend that ships the word 'undefined' to users on a primary tab.
